Diagnosis:

1. The failing test case creates a StrBuilder with the content "\n%BLAH%\nDo more stuff\neven more stuff\n%BLAH%\n".
2. It calls deleteAll("\n%BLAH%") on that StrBuilder.
3. The method StrBuilder.deleteAll(String) does the following:
   - It gets the length of the input string to delete.
   - It finds the first occurrence of that string using indexOf(str, 0).
   - In a loop, while indexOf returns a valid index, it calls deleteImpl(index, index + len, len) to delete the substring, then looks for the next occurrence starting from the same index.
4. The deleteImpl method uses System.arraycopy to move characters in the buffer array to delete the substring and adjusts the size.
5. The indexOf method searches for the substring starting at the given index, returning the position if found, else -1.
6. The bug report states that deleteAll and replaceAll methods can throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
7. The failure likely comes from the fact that after deleting a substring from the buffer, the subsequent call to indexOf(str, index) starts the search from the same index where the previous deletion ended, which can cause overlapping or skipping parts of the string.
8. Moreover, when multiple adjacent or overlapping occurrences of the substring exist, always starting the search from the same index after deletion can result in an infinite loop or index corruption.
9. The use of System.arraycopy in deleteImpl may result in out-of-bounds access if indices are not properly handled, especially if the size or buffer length is not updated correctly after deletion.
10. Specifically, in the test "\n%BLAH%\nDo more stuff\neven more stuff\n%BLAH%\n", deleting all occurrences of "\n%BLAH%" will cause the method to try to handle deletions at positions that shift after each deletion, but the current algorithm does not account for this shift properly when searching the next index.
11. This results in an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException during the array copy in deleteImpl or during the indexOf method's internal operations.

In conclusion, the current implementation of deleteAll deletes substrings correctly only if they are non-overlapping and properly spaced, but fails when the substring occurs multiple times or overlaps after each deletion because the next search index is not updated to reflect the changed buffer content and size. This leads to array index errors.

Recent bug reports don't mention similar index or offset issues in this class, so the problem is specific to deleteAll and how it handles its loop and indexing after deletions.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.deleteAll(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.deleteImpl(int,int,int)
